blockers.summary: Reviewer requests changes: "…The description seems a bit unfinished, please update…" (obondarev)

The fix is a new feature (an RFE adding OVN Address_Set support for address groups) backported to stable branches, which may not qualify as an SRU. No justification, test plan or regression analysis has been provided.

The backport depends on new ovsdbapp Address_Set API support (ovsdbapp review 905044). The Yoga backport was abandoned because of this dependency and later because it 'just won't work on Yoga'. Series with older ovsdbapp may be unable to take the fix without a matching ovsdbapp SRU or version bump.
Backports landed only on stable/2024.2 and stable/2024.1. The Yoga backport was abandoned and there is no sign of backports for other series. It is unclear which Ubuntu series can receive the fix.

The stable backports had conflicts in the functional tests and release note, and the feature changes how ACLs are generated in the OVN driver. Upgrade and existing-ACL handling (e.g. address groups already in use) is not discussed, which creates regression risk.

bugs.title: [OVN] packet drops when provider network MTU exceeds tenant network MTU

blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…two commits in one to not introduce a regression by doing them separately. There were small changes required to unit tes…" (hudson-openstack)

The stable/2024.2 and stable/2024.1 backports are deliberately squashed from two commits (the gateway_mtu change plus the network IDs filter revert for bug 2105383). An Ubuntu SRU must carry both, or it introduces a redirect-type regression.

The upstream fix only takes effect when the non-default option ovn.ovn_emit_need_to_frag is set, and it relies on OVN support for gateway_mtu. The test plan must enable that option and use a suitable OVN version; otherwise the fix cannot be verified and default behaviour does not change.

Upstream backports exist only for stable/2025.1, 2024.2 and 2024.1. If the SRU targets an older Ubuntu series (for example jammy/Yoga or 2023.x), no upstream backport exists, and nothing in the thread shows an Ubuntu package patch, a merge proposal, or verification.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html
